sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the inner Campania region, east of the city of Benevento and toward the northern flank of the Vulture volcano (to the east), and belongs to the oblique to right-lateral strike-slip system that affects the central and southern Adriatic foreland. This Source is a near-vertical, ca. N-dipping, fault to the east of the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a remarkable concentration of catastrophic earthquakes in this region. From west to east, these are: the multiple earthquake that occurred on 21 August 1962 (Mw 6.2, Irpinia); 14 March 1702 (Mw 6.3, Sannio-Irpinia), 29 November 1732 (Mw 6.6, Irpinia), 989 A.D. (Mw 6.0, Irpinia), and the 23 July 1930 (Mw 6.7, Irpinia) earthquakes.
This source is thought to be a deep, blind WNW-ESE trending fault system, a part of the tectonic mechanism that seems to characterize the entire seismogenic domain east of the southern Apennines backbone, and possibly of the central ones too. The western sector of this Source includes the causative fault of the 1732 earthquake, based on field and geomorphological data that locally suggest ground deformation. The western sector includes the fault responsible for the 1930 earthquake, for which recent work by Pino et al. (2008) has established a thoroughly revised fault plane solution and source parameters. The remarkable concentration of catastrophic earthquakes in the overall area surrounding this region not only poses very complex issues concerning coexisting tectonic mechanisms that can account for the total release seismic moment and the dynamic of fault interaction (if any, and at what depth).
To the west, this source borders the shallower, NW-SE trending, main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
The two main segments of this Source have been associated with the key earthquakes of this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped subsurface structures. The dip was based on seismological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents oblique right-lateral strike slip, based on seismological dat. The minimum and maximum depth were based on seismological and subsurface data. The slip rate was inferred from geodynamic considerations for the tectonic environment that includes this Source.
